title: Sir Jim Ratcliffe holds 'robust' talks with Manchester United fans over ticket prices after the Ineos chief warned of the need to raise funds amid the club's financial issues
text:
Man United increased fears on more ticket price increases in a statement last month Manchester United Supporters Trust has urged freezing in ticket prices Listen now: Everything is starting! Will Everton Blow Liverpool recover in the week defined by the season? By Liam Morgan
Published: 19:55 GMT, February 13, 2025 | Updated: 00:28 GMT, February 14, 2025
Sir Jim Ratcliffe has held solid conversations with Manchester United fans for ticket prices after the billionaire warned about the need to raise funds during a meeting in Carrington on Thursday.
Ratcliffe, 72, met with the Fan Advisory Board to listen to the opinions of the followers, since the club considers its focus during the season tickets next season. Fans are concerned about costs will increase after the controversial decision to increase the price of seats for certain matches to £ 66 and AX concessions in the middle of the campaign.
The financial problems of United have led Ratcliffe and ineos to eliminate 250 jobs in the club and Mail Sport reported last week that other staff of more than 100 is ready to free money for the expenditure of the first team.
The problems have also caused fears of more walks for the 2025-26 and Mail Sport season understand that, although no concrete decisions were made, the representatives of the fans were firm in their views to Ratcliffe on the subject of the prices of the prices of Tickets.
The manufacturers were eager to emphasize how to boost important decisions on tickets without consultation, as happened with the increase of £ 66, it would be counterproductive and the need to interact with fans.
It is understood that the head of INEOS took the opinions of the FAB of 13 members on board, while the supporters heard Ratcliffe’s opinions about the financial challenges raised by the club, but they argued robust that it would be counterproductive to connect the income gap with higher prices .

The meeting was the second between FAB and Ratcliffe, who has injected £ 241 million into the club since his investment was confirmed in December 2023, after they held face -to -face conversations last year. The dialogue is expected to continue before United announce the renovations process for the next season.
Relations between United and Ratcliffe fans have worsened considerably in recent months after the walk of £ 66 in the middle of the season and the elimination of concessions for children and pensioners.
The supporters are frustrated because they are asked to pay more while the team continues to fight, with Ruben Amorim’s side at the Premier League table.
During the victory of United in Fulham last month, the visual end expressed his anger with Ratcliffe, calling him a **** and comparing it with the very revealed Glazer family.
In December, Ratcliffe caused fury at the Fans base after an interview that gave United We Stand Fanzine, where he explicitly declared that United should not charge less for tickets than Fulham.
